preamble: The diphthong /aʊ/ reduces to schwa when it loses stress. A clear English case is the second element of compound place names in -mouth: the full word mouth /maʊθ/ is reduced to /məθ/ in Plymouth, Portsmouth, Dartmouth, Exmouth and similar names, which are stressed on the first element. The reduction is lexicalized in these names and does not apply to the free word.

examples.note: The unstressed second element of the compound is reduced to [məθ].
